key_insight: REDAR uses reinforcement learning to select phase-specific distillation strengths, replacing fixed regularisation coefficients in class-incremental learning.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help engineering recognition systems learn new classes while retaining prior knowledge, though solid-mechanics applications are not evaluated.
method: Frame regularisation selection as a sequential decision problem.
Use performance metrics and incoming-data statistics to choose each phase’s distillation coefficients.
Train the policy on pseudo-incremental tasks from initial-phase data, then deploy it without further adaptation.
evidence_signal: On CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet, the abstract reports reduced forgetting, improved forward transfer over fixed and heuristic baselines, and transfer from short training horizons to longer incremental runs.
watch_item: A policy trained only on initial-phase pseudo-tasks may face distribution shifts in later phases; robustness beyond the reported image benchmarks remains untested.
paper_title: REDAR: Reinforcement-Driven Adaptive Regularisation for Class Incremental Learning
